title: The Adorable puppy
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：adorable　|　正文 331 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 adorable 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the writer wrote of ① an adorable puppy in the manuscript, and everybody in the study said at once that it was ② more adorable than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the writer, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the adorable ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most adorable puppy anybody in the study had ever seen, or so the manuscript for January 1948 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too adorable to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the reader who had come to help; the adorable ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the page at the far shelf, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an adorable habit of hers, and said that no reader in his right mind would call it ⑥ as adorable as the habit of hers they had once had in the old study. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was adorable or not, and he said so.

By 1961 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manuscript. What the line asked for was ⑦ something adorable, and nothing besides. The reader from the next study called the whole plan ⑧ quite adorable; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manuscript kept the names of the adorable ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1964, on the same day, she wrote of another adorable puppy in the same manuscript, and the work, which took two months, seemed  more adorable than anybody had expected.  The most adorable habit of hers in the whole study, she said in 1966, was the one she could never quite name; the adorable ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 可爱（前置定语 an adorable puppy：1954 年写作者在手稿里记下的那件可爱的小狗）
B. adj. 可爱／讨人喜欢（比较级 more adorable than：文中两处，一处比小狗，一处比预想）
C. adj. 可爱／讨人喜欢（最高级 the most adorable：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 可爱（表语 too adorable to do：母亲觉得它太可爱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 讨人喜欢（前置定语 an adorable habit of hers：叔叔把整件事称作一桩讨人喜欢的小习惯）
F. adj. 讨人喜欢（同级比较 as adorable as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩她的小习惯相比）
G. adj. 讨人喜欢（后置定语 something adorable：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 讨人喜欢（受程度副词修饰 quite adorable：那位读者的评价）

answers.why: adorable 意为“可爱”，1954 年写作者在手稿里记下的是“一件可爱的小狗”，此处作前置定语 an adorable puppy。
adorable 意为“可爱”，此处用比较级 more adorable than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
adorable 意为“可爱”，手稿上 一月 那行字说它是书斋里最可爱的一件，故用最高级 the most adorable puppy。
adorable 意为“可爱”，母亲认为这件东西“太可爱了，谁也用不上”，too adorable to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
adorable 意为“讨人喜欢”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩讨人喜欢的小习惯”，此处作前置定语 an adorable habit of hers。
adorable 意为“讨人喜欢”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩她的小习惯一样讨人喜欢”，同级比较用 as adorable as。
adorable 意为“讨人喜欢”，手稿上那半行字要的是“讨人喜欢的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something adorable。
adorable 意为“讨人喜欢”，邻书斋来的那位读者认为这套计划“相当讨人喜欢”，quite 修饰原级 adorable。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年，写作者在手稿里记下了一件可爱的小狗。（an adorable puppy）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更可爱。（more adorable than …）
母亲觉得它太可爱，谁也用不上。（too adorable to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩讨人喜欢的小习惯。（an adorable habit of hers）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩她的小习惯一样讨人喜欢。（as adorable as …）
到了 1961 年，手稿上只剩半行字：要的是一件讨人喜欢的东西。（something adorable）
answers: In 1954 the writer wrote of an adorable puppy in the manuscript.
Everybody said it was more adorable than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too adorable to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an adorable habit of hers.
He said nobody would call it as adorable as the habit of hers they had once had.
By 1961 the manuscript asked for nothing but something adorable.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 adorable 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the writer wrote of an adorable puppy in the manuscript, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most adorable puppy in the study, or so the manuscript says.
My mother thought it too adorable to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an adorable habit of hers, and nobody argued with him.
The reader from the next study called the plan quite adorable, and everybody laughed.
The adorable ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
